_comment: Adjudicated ACC diagnostic cases -> regression fixtures + institutional ACC knowledge (Ed/ChatGPT 2026-09-19). Each is the INTENDED V2 outcome given the real evidence + Bedrock policy, keyed to the real acc_decisions row. Bedrock policy encoded here: a missing SIGNATURE is an ADMINISTRATIVE deficiency, NOT substantive grounds to deny — Miranda performs the substantive review, records administrative_status=PENDING_SIGNATURE, obtains the signature from the homeowner herself, and completes automatically; no human escalation merely for a missing signature. administrative_status is a forthcoming contract field (keep administrative completeness separate from substantive ACC compliance); the executable regression runner + that contract field land AFTER the V2 dry-run results are reviewed, so the running experiment stays clean.

policy.administrative_vs_substantive: Administrative completeness (signature, dates, owner acknowledgment, contractor info) is tracked separately from substantive architectural compliance and must not contaminate the substantive decision.
policy.missing_signature: administrative deficiency -> substantive review proceeds; administrative_status=PENDING_SIGNATURE; Miranda CONTACTS THE HOMEOWNER to collect THEIR signature, records/attaches it, then auto-resumes and completes. She never signs or attests on the homeowner's behalf. Not an escalation.
policy.curing_condition: A currently-noncompliant-but-curable item is APPROVE_WITH_CONDITIONS with a specific curing condition (e.g. 'relocate shed to maintain the required 5ft setback'), never an uncured approval and not an automatic denial.
policy.subjective_standard: Resolve via community precedent + available evidence; escalate only if genuinely unresolved after that.

fixtures.project: Roof-mounted solar panel + Tesla Powerwall battery

expected.objective_findings: roof-mounted solar is a permitted device; screening/visibility governs, not prohibition
curing_conditions: panels installed to minimize visual impact per guidelines
expected.note: V1 said NEED_INFO partly because the application PDF failed to read — an EVIDENCE/ingestion issue, not judgment. With the PDF read, this should resolve to APPROVE_WITH_CONDITIONS.

fixtures.project: Exterior masonry repair — brick + roof-to-wall flashing

expected.objective_findings: brick product documented (brand/line/color) and cleared; flashing is like-for-like repair
curing_conditions: repaired/replaced materials must match existing exterior in color, finish, and coursing

fixtures.project: In-ground pool 21'4" x 10'6", Tahiti blue interior

expected.objective_findings: in-ground is permitted; colors resolvable via precedent; barrier is code, curable by condition
curing_conditions: pool + equipment must meet required setbacks and not encroach easements

fixtures.project: Freestanding louvered pergola patio cover, gray metal

expected.objective_findings: peak height ~8.2ft <= 12ft (COMPLIES); patio covers permitted; materials-complement resolvable via precedent
curing_conditions: metal frame painted an approved color
maintain positive drainage / no runoff onto adjacent property

fixtures.project: Exterior repaint, Benjamin Moore Barbados Sand 1094 (match existing)

governing_requirements: color change requires ACC approval; same-color repaint needs none
expected.objective_findings: brand + color name + code provided; matches existing; precedent supports
expected.note: The clean case V1 already handled correctly — Miranda, verifier, and human all aligned including the condition (Barbados Sand 1094 / match existing).

fixtures.project: Oak tree trimming + front yard lawn re-sod
fixtures.adjudication: Miranda was correct: the application was genuinely UNSIGNED and UNDATED (verified against the PDF). Per Bedrock policy this is administrative, not a denial.

governing_requirements: tree trimming scope per arborist standards
expected.objective_findings: sod species must be an approved variety (curable by condition); trimming scope resolvable; SIGNATURE MISSING = administrative only
curing_conditions: sod must be an ACC-approved turfgrass variety
expected.expected_escalation: none — Miranda contacts the homeowner to collect THEIR signature, records it, and auto-completes (she never signs on their behalf); a missing signature is NOT substantive grounds to deny or to escalate
